title: kv-cache: improved memory manager and eviction scheduler for spillover/defrag heuristics
author: Sofia Chen
description: Motivation: KV cache memory pressure in high-concurrency workloads leads to excessive paging and fragmentation, increasing latency tail and token-cost. This PR implements a memory manager and eviction scheduler that: 1) prioritizes defragmentation-friendly evictions to reduce long-term fragmentation; 2) delays spillover paging for short-lived spikes by using an adaptive headroom budget per-GPU; 3) introduces an eviction priority that combines recency, entry-size, and hotness score to avoid evicting many small entries that cause compaction churn; 4) offloads background compaction/async spill tasks to a rate-limited scheduler to avoid interfering with latency-critical inference paths. Changes: - new kv/memory_manager.{h,cc}: central policy for tracking memory buckets, fragmentation metrics, per-GPU headroom, and admission control for spillover; - kv/eviction_scheduler.{h,cc}: implements prioritized eviction queues, composite scoring (LRU * size_penalty * hotness_boost), and a leaky-bucket rate limiter for async compaction; - runtime/kv_cache.cc: integration hooks for cooperative eviction points, non-blocking async spill API, and KV lookup fast-path adjustments to consult headroom signals; - tests/kv_cache_memory_manager_test.cc: deterministic unit tests for fragmentation and paging behaviors; - perf/bench/kv-eviction-bench.cc: microbench harness used to validate tail latency improvements; - docs/ops/kv-eviction.md: operator-facing description of new config knobs and migration notes. Compatibility: default policy is backwards-compatible; new behavior is gated behind a runtime flag (kv.enable_adaptive_memory_manager) which is enabled on rollout after canary. Benchmarks: internal benchmarking (see perf/bench results) shows 18-28% tail P99 latency reduction on multi-request workloads and 12% average token-cost reduction under heavy cache churn. Rollout plan: staged canary (10% traffic) -> 50% -> full, with automatic rollback on error-rate regression. Related work items: ENG-4213 (memory manager design), ENG-4289 (eviction scoring), incident INT-99 (production memory pressure report).

review_comments: Asha Patel: Great decomposition. Please add a small comment explaining why we use a size_penalty linear vs log - risk of starving medium entries.
Sofia Chen: Added comment and a microbenchmark in bench to show linear penalty avoids pathological promotion in our trace profiles.
Miguel Rivera: Can we avoid shared mutex on the hot-path? The fast-path changes still take a brief lock. Consider RCU or snapshotting metadata.
Sofia Chen: Reworked fast-path to use atomic snapshot for headroom and a lock-free min-check; kept lock for slow-path eviction only. Added explanation in comments and unit tests simulate contention.
Liam O'Connor (approval): Verified perf numbers in canary harness, code looks good. Recommend squash-merge.
Infra-CI: flake detected in one test on older GCC, reran and passed.
release_notes: Improve KV cache memory management: adaptive headroom, defrag-aware eviction scoring, and background compaction scheduler. Expected P99 latency reduction under heavy churn and lower token-costs. Gated behind kv.enable_adaptive_memory_manager flag for staged rollout.
notes_for_ops: Operators: new config knobs under runtime.kv.memory_manager.*. Default conservative settings enabled. Recommended to monitor kv.memory.headroom_ratio, kv.eviction.compaction_rate, and tail latency after rollout. Rolling upgrade supported; nodes can flip flag independently. See docs/ops/kv-eviction.md for escalation steps.
post_merge_actions: Schedule full cluster canary for 11/13, monitor ENG-4289 dashboards, run chaos + mem-pressure job. Backport plans: target release/2025-11-hotfix if regression reported.
